This was, to a large extent, apparent across the market but pricing pressure was most severe in short tail books in particular the Property, Marine & Energy divisions, and led to deteriorating results, necessitating an increase in loss reserves across these lines of business.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a significant gross strengthening of reserves by GBP 290.7 million for underwriting years prior to 2018, representing 37.64% of opening gross reserves. This adverse development was primarily driven by the need to further strengthen reserves on business written prior to 2018, particularly in short-tail lines such as North American property and Marine. This was influenced by intense market competition and pricing pressure from 2012 to 2016, which led to deteriorating results. Catastrophe events from 2017 (Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Maria, California wildfires) and 2016 (Texas hailstorms, Louisiana flooding, Hurricane Matthew) also contributed to the impact on prior year accounts.

data.data_quality_notes: The prior year development was calculated from the gross claims development table for underwriting years <= 2016, as no explicit "Movement in prior year's provision" note was found. The narrative on page 42 mentions a "net overall improvement of GBP 11.3m" which differs significantly from the gross strengthening calculated from the triangle, suggesting different scopes or definitions. The triangle calculation is for gross cumulative incurred claims for specific UW years, while the narrative might refer to a net P&L impact.
